The post holders will spearhead projects in large-scale cancer genomics and evolution. The Cancer Genomics and Evolution laboratory Our research focuses on large-scale pan-cancer genomics to gain insight into the genes, mutational processes and evolution of cancer. Our work is highly data-driven, with a focus on large-scale data analysis to gain broad biological insight and on the development of computational methods to enable conceptually novel analyses. The research group is mostly computational with a small wet-lab component. Since its inception, members of the Cancer Genomics and Evolution laboratory have co-authored 22 papers in Nature, Cell or Science. Recent successes include studies of intra-tumor heterogeneity across cancers (Dentro et al., Cell 2021), the evolutionary history of cancer (Gerstung et al., Nature 2020), biallelic mutations in cancer genomes (Demeulemeester et al., Nature Genetics 2022), combined DNA methylation and genomic alterations in lung cancer evolution (Gimeno-Valiente et al., Nature Genetics 2025), benchmarking methods for subclonal reconstruction (Salcedo et al., Nature Biotechnology 2025), and the history of chromosomal instability in genome doubled tumors (Baker et al., Cancer Discovery 2024). Position qualifications The ideal candidate will have a PhD in computational biology (bioinformatics, genomics, …) and research experience in the field of cancer genomics, although we welcome applications from candidates with diverse educational backgrounds, including computational biology, physics and (bio)statistics, biology or medicine. Applicants must have a proven publication record. Prior experience with handling massively parallel sequencing data is considered an advantage. Postdocs will spearhead projects in cancer genomics and tumor evolution. They are expected to lead their own project, contribute to other projects on a collaborative basis (both within the lab and with external collaborators) and guide PhD students in their research. The ability to work in a team is essential. The laboratory conducts NIH-funded research at the intersection of immunology, stem cell biology, regenerative medicine, aging, autoimmunity, and cancer immunology. Our laboratory investigates fundamental mechanisms regulating T-cell development, thymic function, immune tolerance, and immune aging, with the goal of translating these discoveries into novel cell- and protein-based therapies. The laboratory currently has NIH-funded research projects and provides a highly collaborative environment for postdoctoral training and career development. Research Areas Current research projects include: 1. Stem cell–based thymic regeneration and immune tolerance We use embryonic stem cells (ESCs) and induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) to generate thymic epithelial progenitors (TEPs) and thymic epithelial cells (TECs). These studies investigate mechanisms of thymic epithelial development and explore the therapeutic potential of ESC/iPSC-derived cells for restoring T-cell immunity during aging and genetic immunodeficiency and for inducing antigen-specific immune tolerance in autoimmune diseases. 2. Recombinant protein therapeutics for immune aging and age-related disease We use protein engineering to develop recombinant FOXN1 fusion proteins that promote thymic regeneration and T-cell development. Current studies investigate their therapeutic potential in age-related T-cell immunodeficiency and other age-associated pathologies. 3. Novel immune checkpoint pathways in autoimmunity and cancer Using bioinformatics, molecular biology, and protein engineering, we have identified novel immune regulatory molecules, including ERMAP and TAPBPL. Current studies investigate their receptors, signaling mechanisms, and therapeutic potential using recombinant proteins and antibodies in animal models of autoimmune disease and cancer. The successful candidate will participate in one or more of these research programs depending on experience and scientific interests. Responsibilities Design and conduct research experiments; Perform cellular, molecular, and immunological studies; Work with ESCs/iPSCs and differentiated cell populations, depending on the project; Perform flow cytometry and functional immune-cell assays; Conduct molecular biology, protein, and gene-expression analyses; Use mouse models of immune-mediated and other human diseases; Analyze and interpret experimental data; Assist with mentoring graduate and undergraduate researchers as appropriate. Qualifications Required qualifications: Ph.D., M.D., M.D./Ph.D., or equivalent doctoral degree in immunology, cell biology, molecular biology, stem cell biology, biomedical sciences, or a related discipline; Strong research experience and evidence of scientific productivity; Ability to design experiments, analyze data, and work independently; Ability to work effectively in a collaborative research environment. Experience in one or more of the following areas is highly desirable: Immunology and T-cell biology; Flow cytometry and cell sorting; Mammalian cell culture; ESC or iPSC culture and differentiation; Molecular and cellular biology; Recombinant protein expression and protein engineering; Gene editing, including CRISPR/Cas9; Mouse genetics, mouse colony management, and in vivo disease models; Autoimmunity, cancer immunology, neuroimmunology, or aging research; Histology, immunofluorescence, or confocal microscopy; and Bioinformatics or analysis of high-dimensional biological data. Candidates are not expected to have expertise in all of these areas. Research Environment UConn provides a multidisciplinary research environment with resources and core facilities supporting flow cytometry, stem cell research, genomics, proteomics, microscopy, animal models, and mouse genome modification. The laboratory maintains collaborations with investigators at UConn and other national and international institutions. The Storrs campus is located in Connecticut with access to the broader biomedical research communities in Connecticut, Boston, and New York. Application Interested candidates should submit: A cover letter describing research experience, scientific interests, and career goals; A current CV, including a publication list; and Names and contact information for three references. Jointly offered by the Max Planck Society (MPG; https://www.mpg.de/en) and the Weizmann Institute of Science (WIS; https://www.weizmann.ac.il/pages/), this prestigious program provides a comprehensive four-year position in a unique research environment. About The Program MPG, based in Germany, and WIS, located in Israel, have joined forces to offer an exceptional postdoctoral program that promotes scientific collaboration and fosters interdisciplinary research. This program provides an outstanding opportunity for talented researchers to engage in cutting-edge projects, benefit from the expertise of two world-renowned institutions, and contribute to advancing knowledge in their respective fields. Program Highlights 1. Duration: Our joint postdoctoral program has a duration of four years, with an equal distribution of time between MPG and WIS. This unique structure allows postdoctoral fellows to benefit from the expertise and resources available at both institutions, fostering a rich and diverse research experience by ensuring dedicated time for in-depth exploration, comprehensive experimentation and significant contributions to their respective fields. 2. Eligibility Criteria: a. Applicants must start the program within 4 years of their Ph.D. graduation b.Current WIS postdocs are eligible to apply, but must commence the program before the end of their first year at WIS c. Commencement into the program is contingent upon PhD thesis submission 3. Fellowships: During their time at MPG, postdocs positions are according to the German regulations and guidelines, and based on the experience level (German level 2 or level 3). Specific annual taxable salary levels are €67,311 for level 2 and €72,800 for level 3. This includes benefits such as health insurance, nursing care insurance, vacation days, pension insurance, and unemployment insurance. During their time at WIS, postdocs will receive an untaxed fellowship of 212,088 NIS annually for level 2 and 220,920 NIS annually for level 3. * Postdoctoral fellows in Israel are exempt from taxes. In addition, at WIS, Postdocs will receive full family health insurance, nursing care subsidy, vacation days, relocation expenses and subsidized housing. The relocation expenses will be paid by the host Institution to which the fellow is relocating, and up to twice during the program (with a minimum of 18 months in between). The expenses are at the level of €1500 for single postdocs per relocation, and €3000 for postdocs with spouses and families. 4. Global Research Collaboration: Fellows will have the opportunity to collaborate with leading scientists from both MPG and WIS. This program promotes a global research network, facilitating the exchange of ideas, expertise and diverse perspectives. 5. Independent Travel Support: We understand the importance of scientific networking and dissemination of research findings. As part of this program, fellows will receive up to 3000 Euros per year for conferences, workshops and seminars, enabling them to present their work, engage with peers, and establish valuable professional connections. Application Process To apply for the MPG-WIS Joint Postdoctoral Program, please follow the application guidelines below: - Contact researchers at MPG (see list of institutions; https://www.weizmann.ac.il/sites/mpg-wis/application-process#block-wis-theme-views-block-list-of-mpg-institutions-block-1) and at WIS; (https://www.weizmann.ac.il/pages/science/research), to discuss potential collaborative projects for which the researchers from both institutions can serve as joint hosts. - Provide a detailed CV highlighting your academic background, research experience, list of publications, list of invited talks, awards, and any other relevant information specific to your field of research. - Arrange for at least three letters of recommendation (one should be from the PhD advisor). These letters should come from individuals familiar with your research work and can assess your potential as a postdoctoral researcher in your specific field. - Support letters from the MPG and WIS host researchers (can be a joint letter). Please note: as at each institute the costs are split between the institute and the PI, the PIs should declare that they have available funds to support the candidate. - A Research statement explaining the project and its collaborative nature between the MPG and WIS (Length: up to 2 pages, Margins: 2 cm, Font size: 11 pt) - A statement about the planned split between the institutes (MPG and WIS) for the duration of the 4 years. This should indicate at which institute (MPG or WIS) you will begin your four-year position. The four years should be split equally between the institutions. Several transfers are allowed, but generally not for a duration of less than a year. This plan should be based on scientific justification given the expertise and infrastructure at both institutions. This plan can be changed during the program upon the program committee approval. - Upon completing the session and clicking the “Submit Application” button, you will receive an email verifying your application. Please note: this email also contains unique links for each of the referees you have listed. You may send each referee their unique link, which will allow them to access the system and submit their letter of recommendation. For inquiries and assistance regarding the joint postdoctoral program offered by the MPG and WIS, please reach out to our program coordinator, Ms. Livnat Moses. Livnat will be your main point of contact and will provide guidance throughout the application process and during your participation in the program. You can contact the program coordinator via the following channels: Email: postdoc@weizmann.ac.il Phone: +972-8-9343842 Application Deadline: 1 December 2026, for positions starting between March 2027 and September 2027.
